title: Casablanca
why: Love, sacrifice, and some of the most quoted lines ever written. A wartime café drama that still plays like it was made yesterday.

title: Citizen Kane
why: A 25-year-old first-time director reinvented how movies could look and tell a story. Watch for the deep focus and ceilings in every shot.

title: The Wizard of Oz
why: The jump from sepia to Technicolor is still pure movie magic. Shot on the MGM lot in Culver City.

title: Double Indemnity
why: The blueprint for film noir: an insurance salesman, a femme fatale, and Los Feliz sunshine hiding something rotten.

title: Bicycle Thieves
why: A father and son search postwar Rome for a stolen bike. Simple, devastating, and the heart of Italian neorealism.

title: The Third Man
why: Tilted angles, shadowy Vienna sewers, an unforgettable zither score, and one of cinema's great entrances.

title: Sunset Boulevard
why: Hollywood eats its own. A forgotten silent star and a broke screenwriter in a crumbling mansion off Sunset.

title: Rashomon
why: One crime, four contradictory versions. It gave its name to an entire idea about truth and memory.

title: Singin' in the Rain
why: The most joyful movie ever made about Hollywood switching to sound. The title number alone is worth it.

title: Tokyo Story
why: An elderly couple visits their busy grown-up children. Quiet and patient, and it'll make you call your parents.

title: Seven Samurai
why: Villagers hire masterless samurai to defend their harvest. Every team-up movie since owes it something. Long, and worth every minute.

title: Rear Window
why: A laid-up photographer, a heat wave, and a courtyard full of neighbors' windows. Hitchcock turns you into the snoop.

title: Rebel Without a Cause
why: James Dean defined teenage angst. The Griffith Observatory scenes are why there's a bust of him up there today.

title: Vertigo
why: Obsession in San Francisco. Hypnotic, strange, and often voted the greatest film ever made.

title: Some Like It Hot
why: Two musicians on the run hide in an all-women band. Still one of the funniest movies ever, with a perfect last line.

title: Psycho
why: It broke every rule of what a mainstream movie could do. Go in knowing as little as possible.

title: Lawrence of Arabia
why: The desert as you've never seen it. If it ever plays in 70mm near you, go.

title: 8½
why: A director who can't figure out his next movie. Dreamlike, funny, and endlessly copied.

title: Dr. Strangelove
why: A pitch-black comedy about nuclear annihilation, with Peter Sellers playing three roles.

title: The Graduate
why: Post-college drift in sunny suburban LA, set to Simon & Garfunkel. The final shot is perfect.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
why: From apes to the infinite in one cut. See it on the biggest screen you can find.

title: The Godfather
why: Family, power, and America, told like an opera. It earns every one of its three hours.

title: Chinatown
why: The ultimate LA movie, a noir about who controls the water. You'll never see the city's history the same way.

title: Jaws
why: The original summer blockbuster. Two notes of music and you'll think twice before going in the water.

title: Taxi Driver
why: A lonely night-shift cabbie in 1970s New York. Unsettling, and anchored by one of the great screen performances.

title: Star Wars
why: A farm boy, a princess, a smuggler, and a galaxy. It changed what movies could be and who went to see them.

title: Halloween
why: The slasher that started it all, made for almost nothing. Set in Illinois, but those leafy streets are South Pasadena.

title: Alien
why: Haunted house in space. Slow, grimy, terrifying, and Ripley rewrote the action hero.

title: Apocalypse Now
why: A journey upriver into the madness of the Vietnam War. Overwhelming in the best way.

title: The Shining
why: A snowed-in hotel and a family coming apart. Every hallway is a nightmare.

title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
why: As close to a perfect adventure movie as anyone has made. Pure fun from the first boulder.

title: Blade Runner
why: Rainy, neon, future LA. Its look shaped decades of sci-fi. Spot the Bradbury Building downtown.

title: Back to the Future
why: A tightly built crowd-pleaser where every setup pays off. Doc's house is Pasadena's Gamble House.

title: The Princess Bride
why: Fencing, fighting, true love, and miracles. Endlessly quotable for kids and adults.

title: My Neighbor Totoro
why: Two sisters, a countryside summer, and a giant fuzzy forest spirit. Gentle, wondrous, and with no villain at all.

title: Do the Right Thing
why: The hottest day of the year on one Brooklyn block. Funny, vibrant, and still urgent.

title: Goodfellas
why: Thirty years in the mob at breakneck speed. That Copacabana tracking shot is film school in two minutes.

title: Boyz n the Hood
why: Growing up in South Central LA. Singleton was 24 and became the youngest-ever Best Director nominee.

title: Groundhog Day
why: A cynical weatherman relives the same February day over and over. Funnier and wiser every time you rewatch it.

title: Pulp Fiction
why: Scrambled timelines, endless talk, and LA diners. It rewired '90s indie film.

title: The Shawshank Redemption
why: Friendship and hope behind prison walls. It became beloved slowly, one rewatch at a time.

title: Heat
why: Pacino vs. De Niro across a sprawling, nocturnal LA. The downtown shootout is legendary.

title: Toy Story
why: The first fully computer-animated feature, and it holds up because the story is so good.

title: Before Sunrise
why: Two strangers, one night walking around Vienna, just talking. Then watch the two sequels.

title: Fargo
why: A kidnapping goes very wrong in the frozen Midwest. Marge Gunderson is a hero for the ages.

title: The Big Lebowski
why: A bowling, White Russian-drinking slacker gets tangled in a noir plot. A love letter to LA's weirdness.

title: In the Mood for Love
why: Two neighbors in 1960s Hong Kong, longing and restraint. Maybe the most beautiful-looking film ever made.

title: Spirited Away
why: A girl stumbles into a bathhouse for spirits. Endlessly imaginative, and the gateway to all of Studio Ghibli.

title: Amélie
why: A shy Parisian waitress secretly fixes strangers' lives. Whimsical, saturated, and completely charming.

title: Mulholland Drive
why: A dream (or nightmare) about Hollywood. Don't try to solve it on the first watch. Just let it happen.

title: City of God
why: Kids growing up amid gang war in a Rio favela, told with breathless energy.

title: Pan's Labyrinth
why: A dark fairy tale set against Franco's Spain. Gorgeous creatures, real stakes.

title: There Will Be Blood
why: Greed and oil in early California. A towering performance and a score you'll feel in your chest.

title: Moonlight
why: One life in three chapters in Miami. Intimate, tender, and visually stunning.

title: Get Out
why: Meeting the girlfriend's parents goes very wrong. A horror movie with a lot to say, and a modern classic.

title: Parasite
why: Two families, one house, and nothing goes the way you expect. Know nothing before you go in.
